claim.pdf_says: Table 10 - Format 1 picture symbol order of precedence: the 'First Symbol' column-group band spans the 24 symbol columns as Simple, special, and fixed insertion symbols = columns 1-9 (B 0 / , . + +- +- CRDB cs cs); Zero-suppression and floating insertion symbols = columns 10-15 (Z* Z* +- +- cs cs); Other symbols = columns 16-24 (9 A X S V P P 1 N E). The rule between the 'Zero-suppression and floating insertion symbols' band and the 'Other symbols' band falls immediately to the LEFT of the '9' column (verified: vertical rule at x=1696px, '9' cell spans x=1698-1759px).
claim.markdown_says: | | | **Simple, special, and fixed insertion symbols** | | | | | | | | | **Zero-suppression and floating insertion symbols** | | | | | | | **Other symbols** | | | | | | | |  - cell 19 holds '**Other symbols**', but in the symbol-header row directly beneath it cell 19 is 'A X' and cell 18 is '9'. The group label starts one column late, placing the '9' column under 'Zero-suppression and floating insertion symbols'.
claim.why_it_matters: The three band labels are the standard's own classification of the picture symbols. As transcribed, '9' - an ordinary digit-position symbol - is presented as a zero-suppression / floating-insertion symbol, contradicting 13.18.40.5 rule 7 (only 'Z' and '*' are zero-suppression symbols) and rule 6 (only cs, the extended editing sign control symbols, '+' and '-' are floating insertion symbols). Anyone reading the precedence table to derive PICTURE validation would mis-classify the '9' column. The x-mark data itself is correct and unaffected.

verdict.reasoning:
Independently confirmed by pixel analysis of the 300 dpi render and by cell-index enumeration of the markdown; the claim is accurate in every particular.

PDF (E:/Temp/specrecon/v489/spec_p489.png, 2550x3300 @300dpi). Horizontal rules bound the band-label row at y=533..712 and the symbol-header row at y=715..947. Vertical rules that run the full height of the band-label row are at x = 341, 522/533 (double rule closing the 'Second Symbol' stub), 1214, 1696, 2277. Vertical rules spanning the symbol-header row are at x = 534, 619, 683, 746, 809, 885, 961, 1053, 1134, 1214, 1294, 1375, 1455, 1536, 1616, 1696, 1759, 1834, 1897, 1960, 2023, 2088, 2151, 2215, 2277 - exactly 24 cells. Therefore band 1 = x 534-1214 = symbol columns 1-9 (B 0 / , . + +- +- CRDB cs cs); band 2 = x 1214-1696 = columns 10-15 (Z* Z* +- +- cs cs); band 3 = x 1696-2277 = columns 16-24. Column 16 is x 1696-1759, and the glyph printed in it is '9'. The claim's stated coordinates (rule at x=1696, '9' cell 1698-1759) match the measurement. Visual read of the render agrees: 'Other symbols' is centred over the nine-column span that begins with '9'.

Markdown (E:/Temp/specrecon/v489/page-489.md). Every header row has 26 pipe cells; cells 1-2 are the two stub columns and cells 3-26 are the 24 symbol columns. Symbol-header row (line 11): cell 3='B 0 /' ... cell 12='Z *', cell 17='c s', cell 18='9', cell 19='A X' ... cell 26='E'. Band-label row (line 10): labels sit at cell 3, cell 12 and cell 19. Cells 3 and 12 are correct - they are the first column of band 1 (B 0 /) and band 2 (Z *) respectively, establishing the file's own convention that a band label is left-aligned on the band's FIRST column with trailing empty cells for the remainder. By that same convention the third label belongs in cell 18 ('9'); it is in cell 19 ('A X'). The consequence is that the zero-suppression/floating band appears to span 7 columns (Z* Z* +- +- cs cs 9) and 'Other symbols' only 8 (A X S V P P 1 N E), versus 6 and 9 in the PDF.

Refutation attempts, all failed: (a) Not a colspan artefact excusable as formatting - markdown cannot express colspan, but the transcription does encode band extent by label position, and it does so correctly for two of three bands, so the third is an off-by-one, not a notation limit. (b) Not a centring convention - bands 1 and 2 are demonstrably left-aligned, so cell 19 is inconsistent with the file itself. (c) The label text is not merely reflowed onto an adjacent line; it is present, complete, and in the wrong column. (d) Row-stub band labels (line 12 cell 1, line 21 cell 1) are correctly placed, so the error is isolated to the column band. (e) Meaning does change: '9' is classified as a zero-suppression / floating insertion symbol, which 13.18.40.5 rule 7 ('The symbols Z and * are used as the symbols for zero suppression with replacement') and rule 6 ('The currency symbol, the extended editing sign control symbols, if specified, and the fixed editing sign control symbols + and - are used as the floating insertion symbols') both contradict - I read both rules in specs/ISO_COBOL.md to confirm the citation.

The x-mark payload is unaffected, as the claim states: spot-checking the first data row (B 0 /), PDF marks columns 1,2,3,5,8,10,11,12,13,14,15,16,17,19,21,23 and the markdown row (line 12) carries x in exactly those 24-column positions.
verdict.corrected_description: Confirmed as described; no correction needed. Precise form: in E:/CobolSharp/specs/ISO_COBOL.md page-489 Table 10, the band-label row places '**Other symbols**' in pipe cell 19, which aligns with symbol column 17 ('A X'). The PDF's band rule falls at x=1696 px (300 dpi), immediately left of symbol column 16 ('9', x 1696-1759), so the label belongs in pipe cell 18. Fix: move '**Other symbols**' one cell left (cell 19 -> cell 18), leaving the trailing empty cell at the end of the row, so that the bands read 9 / 6 / 9 columns as printed instead of 9 / 7 / 8. Only the band-label row needs to change; the symbol-header row and all sixteen x-mark data rows on this page are faithful to the PDF.
